source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Routine crop management includes removing excess leaves that are old, damaged, or diseased, since damaged leaf tissue can both reduce photosynthesis and harbor pests or fungal spores. Farmers should also remove excess suckers (side shoots) from each clump, typically keeping only one or two selected follow-on shoots to become the next generation's fruiting stem, rather than letting the clump become overcrowded, which reduces bunch size and delays fruiting on every stem.

After the fruit bunch has fully emerged and set, the male flower bud (ត្រយ៉ង) hanging below the bunch is cut off. Removing the male bud redirects the plant's energy into fruit filling rather than continued flower production, and also removes a part of the plant that can otherwise attract pests. Once the bunch has finished filling and before it ripens on the stem, farmers commonly wrap the developing bunch in a plastic bag or sleeve to protect it from insect damage, wind scarring, and sunburn.
